summary: LA County tower moved from Blue Ridge to Bodle Peak in 1930, re-erected 1932, then moved to Triunfo Peak; only foundations and piers are described at Bodle today.

facts.design: Steel X-brace tower with an 8x8 observation cabin; register says 60 ft tall, Angeles Adventures says 50 ft
facts.status_note: Tower was dismantled and re-erected on Triunfo Peak; sources describe only foundation ruins and tower piers at Bodle Peak
facts.agency: Los Angeles County Forestry Department (now Los Angeles County Fire Department)

events.note: Tower dismantled at Blue Ridge in 1930 and moved to Bodle Peak; register and Angeles Adventures both give 1930 for the move
Re-assembled at Bodle Peak during 1932 (register Built field gives 1932)
Dismantled at Bodle Peak in 1934 (Triunfo register); Bodle register Removed field also gives 1934
Re-erected on Triunfo Peak; Triunfo register says during 1934, Bodle register says sometime after 1934
Area burned over in the 2018 Woolsey Fire, per the register

evidence.supports: tower moved from Blue Ridge to Bodle Peak in 1930 by the LA County Forestry Department
evidence.quote: In 1930 the LA County Forestry Department moved its fire lookout tower from Blue Ridge in the San Gabriel Mountains to Bodle Peak, in the western side of the Santa Monica Mountains.

evidence.supports: county forester's stated purpose for the move: protect area with summer homes
evidence.quote: a highly hazardous mountain area where there are many summer homes and valuable properties

evidence.supports: 60-foot X-brace steel tower with 8x8 observation cabin, dismantled at Blue Ridge in 1930
evidence.quote: The lookout structure, a 60 foot X-Brace steel tower and an 8x8 observation cabin were dismantled at Blue Ridge on the Angeles National Forest in 1930.

evidence.supports: Angeles Adventures gives tower height as 50 feet
dismantled structure stored at Bodle Peak and re-assembled in 1932
evidence.quote: The dismantled structure was stored at Bodle Peak and re-assembled during 1932.

evidence.supports: area burned in the 2018 Woolsey Fire
evidence.quote: The area was burned over during the 2018 Woolsey Fire.

evidence.quote: The lookout was once again dismantled and re-assembled on Triunfo Peak sometime after 1934.

evidence.quote: The dismantled structure was re-assembled during 1934.

evidence.supports: the structure was dismantled at Bodle Peak in 1934 (Triunfo register)
evidence.quote: were dismantled at Bodle Peak, 4 miles northeast in 1934.

evidence.quote: Ventura County assisted the Los Angeles County Fire Department in putting up the Triunfo Peak lookout in May 1930. In November of that year, the Potrero fire burned 23,000 acres between Thousand Oaks and the coast and incinerated the Triunfo Peak tower.

evidence.quote: The concrete base is of unknown purpose

evidence.quote: The summit is a flat area with small foundation ruins and rocky crags.

evidence.quote: A satellite image show the tower piers still existing and what appears to be a foundation of a residence cabin.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Register gives a 60-foot X-brace tower; Angeles Adventures gives 50 feet. The story reports both and does not choose one, so height_m is omitted.
Angeles Adventures dates the lookout 1930-1934 from the move; the register gives Built 1932 for the re-erection at Bodle Peak. Both are reported separately.

Triunfo register says re-assembled during 1934; Bodle register says sometime after 1934. Reported both ways. The Triunfo register also describes an earlier tower on that summit, built May 1930 and destroyed in the November 1930 Potrero fire, so the story says its dates should be read with care.

notes_for_editor: Height is disputed (60 ft register vs 50 ft Angeles Adventures). Access level is not stated by any source read, so facts.access is omitted. The Woolsey Fire claim rests on the register alone. The register spells Mulholland as 'Muholland' (kept as written in the quote). The register's Halloween 1930 sentence about an earlier timber lookout is left out because it does not say that lookout stood at Bodle. The Triunfo register also says a tower on that summit was built in May 1930 and burned in the November 1930 Potrero fire, which does not square with a Bodle tower arriving in 1934; check before relying on the Triunfo dates. A search summary gave a 50-foot height and a Woolsey claim it could not verify; neither was used.
